analysis.title: Spotlight turns to jobs report after Fed takes a pause (US Macro Weekly, 30 October 2026)
key_insights: CA-CIB forecasts October nonfarm payrolls at +65k, up from +29k in September, with unemployment steady at 4.2% and average hourly earnings +0.3% MoM (YoY edging down to 2.9% from 3.0%). The bank reads this as a labour market in decent shape and close to balance, with the breakeven job-growth rate having dropped sharply.

The October FOMC held the target range at 3.75-4.00% after the 25bp hike in September. Two dissents favoured a hike, and one came from Governor Lisa Cook, which CA-CIB did not expect. CA-CIB had expected three dissents.

Chair Kevin Warsh justified the pause by describing an 'information rich interval' in which the Fed accumulates more data. He gave no forward guidance. CA-CIB rates his tone as less hawkish than Jackson Hole and the September FOMC, and more hawkish than the July FOMC.
CA-CIB's base case is two more 25bp hikes, in December and March, taking the upper bound to 4.50% and reversing the late-2025 insurance cuts. It flags consecutive hikes as a risk.

CA-CIB sees room for modest easing later: two 25bp cuts in Q4 2027 to take the upper bound to 4.00%, once the inflation forecast improves in H2 2027. It argues the neutral rate has moved higher, so easing would be limited.

The FOMC statement added language that 'the accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the Committee's 2 percent goal'. CA-CIB reads this as leaving the door open to more hikes without committing.
Next year the FOMC will keep eight meetings, but one will be a strategy meeting with no rate vote and no policy statement.

JOLTS openings are expected to show a balanced labour market, with the vacancy-to-unemployment ratio near 1x and a historically low layoffs rate. CA-CIB expects nothing that would worry the Fed, whose focus stays on inflation.
CA-CIB expects both ISM readings to stay solidly in expansion in October: manufacturing 54.4 (prior 54.5) and services 55.0 (prior 54.9).

Market pricing before the FOMC: a December hike was priced at 77.9% for the 375-400 to 400-425 move, with more than three hikes priced by Q3 2027, up from just under three the prior Friday. From last Friday's close to mid-day Wednesday the 2Y yield rose about 9bp to 4.77% from 4.68%, the 10Y rose a little over 3bp to 5.03% from 5.00%, and the S&P 500 rose 1.4%.

Data in the week before the report was solid. Durable goods orders rose 1.8% MoM in September, core capital goods orders rose 0.5% and shipments 1.2%. Conference Board consumer confidence jumped to 91.7 from an upwardly revised 84.2. New home sales fell 0.6% to 676k.

CA-CIB's macro forecasts: 2026 GDP growth 2.3%, cut from 2.5% because of the Iran war drag, and 2.1% in 2027. Headline CPI peaks at 4.2% YoY in May and stays above 3.0% into early 2027. Core CPI stays around 2.4-2.7% through early 2027. Unemployment is expected to stay in the low 4% range.

CA-CIB's base case for the midterm elections on Nov 3 is Democratic victories in both the House and Senate, with the Senate the closer call, likely leading to legislative gridlock. Oil prices stay elevated with no sign of near-term resolution in the Middle East.
UofM consumer sentiment is forecast flat at 48.0 in the preliminary November reading, still extremely weak, though CA-CIB notes that sentiment has been a poor guide to spending recently.
September factory orders are forecast at +1.8% MoM and the September trade deficit at $108.4bn, from $105.6bn in August. Net exports were a large drag on Q3 2026 GDP.

risk_factors: Consecutive Fed hikes in December and January/March are a risk to CA-CIB's base case.
Energy-driven inflation from the Iran war adds upside risk to CPI forecasts.
AI replacing job functions could weigh on the labour market.
The K-shaped economy, with growth concentrated in AI-related investment, is a risk to growth.
Consumer sentiment is near rock-bottom levels, though CA-CIB notes its link to spending is weak.
vol_and_positioning: The market priced a December Fed hike at 77.9% (14.2% for no change) as of Oct 28, and more than three hikes by Q3 2027, up from just under three the prior Friday.
geopolitical: The Iran war weighs on 2026 US growth, and CA-CIB lowered its 2026 growth forecast to 2.3% from 2.5%.
There is little sign of near-term resolution in the Middle East, which keeps oil prices elevated.
US midterm elections on Nov 3: CA-CIB's base case is Democratic wins in both the House and Senate, with the Senate closer, likely leading to legislative gridlock.
